advice.advice: See the doctor: a vitamin D supplement course is usually needed at this level.
Keep to light or moderate exercise (walking, yoga, easy cycling) until haemoglobin improves; stop if you feel breathless or dizzy.

Eat iron-rich food every day: palak and other greens, rajma, chana, sprouts, ragi, dates, jaggery; eggs, chicken or fish if non-vegetarian. Take a vitamin C food with meals (lemon, amla, guava, orange) and keep tea and coffee an hour away from meals.
advice.mess_tip: Choose dal, palak or rajma curries and the egg dishes where offered; add lemon at lunch.

advice.advice: Iron stores are low: follow the iron-rich food advice daily for at least three months.
advice.mess_tip: Prefer greens, dal and egg options in the weekly menu.

advice.advice: Small red cells often mean low iron: include iron-rich foods and vitamin C with meals.
Get 15-20 minutes of sunlight on arms and face between 10 am and 1 pm on most days; play an outdoor sport.
Include milk, curd, eggs and fish where possible; mushrooms dried in the sun help a little.
At least 45 minutes of brisk walking, cycling or swimming five days a week, strength training twice a week, and 8,000-10,000 steps a day.
Fill half the plate with vegetables and salad, keep rice and roti to one moderate serving, choose grilled over fried, and cut sweets, sugary drinks and fried snacks.
advice.mess_tip: Choose stir-fried over deep-fried items; skip the second rice serving.

advice.advice: Combine cardio (30-45 minutes, five days) with strength training (2-3 days) to lower body fat while keeping muscle.
Cut refined sugar, sweets, bakery and fried snacks; eat more fibre (vegetables, dal, whole grains).
Daily brisk walking and core exercises; waist above the cut-off raises the risk of diabetes and heart disease.
150 minutes of aerobic exercise a week (brisk walking, jogging, cycling, sports).
Fewer fried foods, ghee, butter and bakery items; more oats, dal, vegetables, fruit and a handful of nuts; fish twice a week if non-vegetarian.
advice.mess_tip: Prefer grilled, steamed and stir-fried dishes over deep-fried.

advice.advice: Cut sugar, sweets, fruit juices and refined flour (maida); avoid late-night snacking.
Regular aerobic exercise raises HDL: aim for 30 minutes on most days.
Avoid alcohol, fried and very oily food and unnecessary supplements; keep weight in range.
30 minutes of moderate aerobic exercise most days; sleep 7-8 hours; manage exam stress (breathing exercises, yoga).
Less salt: skip pickles, papad, chips and instant noodles; more fruit, vegetables and curd.
advice.mess_tip: Avoid adding extra salt and pickle at the table.

advice.advice: Build stamina slowly: brisk walking or jogging 3-4 times a week, adding intervals (1 minute fast, 2 minutes easy) after a month.
Add strength training for the whole body twice a week, including hand and forearm work.
Stretch for 10 minutes daily, hold each stretch 30 seconds; yoga twice a week.
